description:
FILED s470bk (Opus, 2026-09-05) while shipping #1058, from the same 31-row
probe matrix (that session's scratch/s470bk/p1058/).  PRE-EXISTING and
SILENT: identical on an e73038f tree and after #1058 + #1057.

PERL VIVIFIES AN INTERMEDIATE DEREFERENCE ON A PURE READ.  Measured, 5.40.3:

  my %h; my $v = $h{a}{b};          perl keys %h = 1   PCL 0
  my %h; my $e = exists $h{a}{b};   perl exists $h{a} = 1, keys 1   PCL 0/0
  my %h; my $d = defined $h{a}{b};  perl 1 / 1                      PCL 0/0
  my %h; my $v = $h{a}{b}{c};       perl keys %h = 1                PCL 0
  my $r; my $v = $r->{p}{q};        perl defined $r = 1             PCL 0
  my %h; $h{a}{b} &&= 5;            perl exists $h{a} = 1           PCL 0
  my %h; my $c = scalar @{$h{a}{b}}; perl exists $h{a} = 1          PCL 0

This is the documented Perl gotcha the CPAN `autovivification` pragma exists
to switch off: "autovivification happens whenever an undefined value is
DEREFERENCED", read or write.  Only the FINAL element of a chain is
lvalue-only -- `my $v = $h{a}` creates nothing.

WHY #1058 DID NOT FIX IT, and why this needs the EMISSION, not the runtime.
`$h{a}{b}` and `$h{a}` both lower the element access to `(p-gethash %h "a")`;
what differs is that in the first the RESULT IS DEREFERENCED.  The runtime
sees only a value, so the inner call cannot know which one it is -- #1058's
fix works precisely because the `-box` chain hands the outer call a PLACE.
So the fix is for the emitter to mark an element access whose result is used
as a container: either lower the intermediate through the vivifying
`-box`/`p-ensure-*` chain (which is what `expand-autoviv` already builds for
`p-setf`, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), or emit a distinct accessor for that
position.  `expand-autoviv` / `expand-autoviv-for-array` is the existing
mechanism and the walker to reuse (rule 11).

WHY IT MATTERS.  It is observable through `keys`, `exists`, `scalar(%h)` and
`each`, and it is the direction that UNDER-creates, so a program that walks
`for my $k (keys %h)` after probing `$h{$k}{x}` sees fewer keys than perl.
Cheap to get wrong in the other direction too: making a read vivify
unconditionally would create keys perl does not (`$h{a}` alone must create
nothing), so the acceptance matrix is the seven rows above PLUS the
"creates nothing" rows: a plain `$h{a}` read, `exists $h{a}`,
`defined $h{a}`, `delete $h{a}{b}` (probe it -- perl DOES vivify $h{a}
there), `$h{a} // 1`, and a read of a THREE-level chain's last element.

BAR when taken: an emission change, so corpus-diff + emission-ab + a
generation bump + artifact regeneration + the full sweep (a read that starts
creating keys can move `keys`/`each` row counts in either direction), the
gate, and rows in Pl/t/autoviv-02.t beside #1058's three.


=== DESIGN (s470br, 2026-09-05), not yet implemented ===
The walker ALREADY EXISTS and must not be copied (rule 11): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's
compile-time `expand-autoviv` / `expand-autoviv-for-array` turn
  (p-gethash %h "a")  ->  (p-autoviv-gethash %h "a")   [returns the HASH]
  (p-gethash %h "a")  ->  (p-autoviv-gethash-for-array %h "a")
and their base case returns the form unchanged, so a BARE container costs
nothing.  p-gethash/p-aref are FUNCTIONS, not macros, so the walker cannot be
reached from them -- hence the emitter.

SHAPE: two new one-line macros in the runtime,
  (defmacro p-viv-container (form) (expand-autoviv form))
  (defmacro p-viv-array-container (form) (expand-autoviv-for-array form))
and in Pl/ExprToCL.pm, `gen_hash_access_form` (line ~3597) and
`gen_array_access_form` (line ~3314) wrap the CONTAINER form in the matching
macro WHEN the container is itself an accessor form -- head one of
p-gethash / p-aref / p-gethash-deref / p-aref-deref -- and NOT in lvalue
context (p-setf already runs expand-autoviv over the whole place).  The same
wrap is needed on the container `_access_container_and_keys` hands the
p-exists arm (ExprToCL line ~2384), which is row 09 of the matrix.

WHY IT IS A BIG CHANGE ANYWAY: it moves the emission of every nested element
READ in the corpus, so it needs the full explain-every-diff pass plus the
sweep (keys/each counts can move in both directions).  s470br stopped here
with #1115 taking the session; the seven residue rows are 08/09/10/21/22/27/28
of the s470bk matrix (archived
~/pcl-agent-scratch/s470/bk-agent-ad0b34477151560d8/s470bk/p1058/).
NOT YET PROBED, and the design needs it before it ships: does perl vivify
BOTH intermediates of $h{a}{b}{c} (row 22 only reports keys %h), and what does
$h{a}{b} &&= 5 (row 27) emit today?

subject: A pure READ of a nested element does not vivify the INTERMEDIATE (perl does): `my $v = $h{a}{b}` leaves keys %h = 0 where perl says 1 - needs the emission, not the runtime
